findings.criterion: Exactly one implementation of "spawn a detached rebar child" exists; the three sites call it and none re-implements the bootstrap or the detach flags.
findings.detail: A fourth detached-rebar-child spawn site exists at `src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py` that independently re-implements the full pattern without calling `rebar._proc.spawn_detached`. It has its own `_detach_kwargs()` function (lines 172–178) referencing `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, its own PYTHONPATH bootstrap (lines 190–194), its own `-c` stub with `sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[3])` (line 204), and its own `subprocess.Popen` call (line 200). The ticket's scope names only three sites, but the criterion requires exactly one implementation to exist — gc_trigger.py is a live fourth copy-paste site.

findings.criterion: A STATIC test (source scan over `src/rebar`) enforces that the signature of a DETACHED-REBAR-CHILD spawn appears only in `_proc.py`
findings.detail: The static test `test_the_detached_spawn_signature_appears_only_in_proc` in `tests/unit/test_spawn_detached.py` (lines 42–57) is correctly written and scans for the tokens `DETACHED_PROCESS`, `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, and `sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv`. However, `src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py` contains all three tokens (lines 176 and 204), so the test would report gc_trigger.py as an offender and FAIL. The test exists but the codebase has a live violation that would cause it to fail.

findings.criterion: `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.
findings.detail: The static test `test_the_detached_spawn_signature_appears_only_in_proc` would fail because `src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py` contains the scanned signature tokens (`DETACHED_PROCESS`, `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, `sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv`) outside of `_proc.py`. The ticket comment claims 232 tests are green, but that attestation predates (or does not account for) the gc_trigger.py violation that the static test is designed to catch.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
